record.context_brief: When two affine connections are dual to each other
record.original_question: Given two affine connections nabla and nabla^* on a manifold M, what conditions ensure that there exists a Riemannian metric g making them dual in the sense that X g(Y, Z) = g(nabla_X Y, Z) + g(Y, nabla^*_X Z)?

evidence.quote: Conversely, suppose that ∇ and ∇∗ are affine connections on M. What is a sufficient condition for two affine connections to be dual to each other? Namely, for two given affine connections ∇ and ∇∗, can we find a Riemannian metric g which satisfies Equation (2)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold equipped with two affine (i.e., torsion-free or general linear) connections $
abla$ and $
abla^{*}$. The pair $(
abla,
abla^{*})$ is said to be dual with respect to a Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ if, for every smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on $M$,
$$X\,g(Y,Z) \;=\; g(
abla_{X}Y,\,Z) \;+\; g(Y,\,
abla^{*}_{X}Z).$$
Determine necessary and/or sufficient conditions on the pair $(
abla,
abla^{*})$ that guarantee the existence of a Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ with respect to which $
abla$ and $
abla^{*}$ are dual in the sense above. Equivalently, characterize those pairs of affine connections on $M$ that arise as a dual pair for some Riemannian metric.
artifact.status_search_result: Standard treatments in information geometry (Amari–Nagaoka and subsequent work) start with a metric $g$ and define the dual connection from it; the converse problem of characterizing when two given affine connections admit a compatible metric making them dual is less standardly resolved. Partial results exist (e.g., on holonomy obstructions for dual connections), but a complete general characterization could not be confirmed from the search.

status_evidence.title: Dual Connections and Holonomy
status_evidence.snippet: Studies obstructions and holonomy aspects related to pairs of dual affine connections.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on obstructions to dual-connection structures exist via holonomy.

status_evidence.title: Methods of Information Geometry (Amari–Nagaoka)
status_evidence.snippet: Dual connections are defined starting from a Riemannian metric; the converse problem is not given a complete general characterization.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference defines duality from a given metric, not the converse.

status_evidence.title: Dual Affine Connections and Dually Flat Manifold
status_evidence.snippet: Develops dual connections assuming a metric is given.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of metric making two given connections dual is not generally characterized.
